title: Delivery Club
statementMd:
Petya and Vasya got employed as couriers. During the working day they are to deliver packages to $*n*$ different points on the line. According to the company's internal rules, the delivery of packages must be carried out strictly in a certain order. Initially, Petya is at the point with the coordinate $*s*_{1}$, Vasya is at the point with the coordinate $*s*_{2}$, and the clients are at the points $*x*_{1}, *x*_{2}, ..., *x*_{*n*}$ in the order of the required visit.

The guys agree in advance who of them will deliver the package to which of the customers, and then they act as follows. When the package for the $*i*$-th client is delivered, the one who delivers the package to the $(*i* + 1)$-st client is sent to the path (it can be the same person who went to the point $*x*_{*i*}$, or the other). The friend who is not busy in delivering the current package, is standing still.

To communicate with each other, the guys have got walkie-talkies. The walkie-talkies work rather poorly at great distances, so Petya and Vasya want to distribute the orders so that the maximum distance between them during the day is as low as possible. Help Petya and Vasya to minimize the maximum distance between them, observing all delivery rules.

## Input

The first line contains three integers $*n*$, $*s*_{1}$, $*s*_{2}$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 100 000$, $0 ≤ *s*_{1}, *s*_{2} ≤ 10^{9}$) — number of points of delivery and starting positions of Petya and Vasya.

The second line contains $*n*$ integers $*x*_{1}, *x*_{2}, ..., *x*_{*n*}$ — customers coordinates ($0 ≤ *x*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$), in the order to make a delivery.

It is guaranteed, that among the numbers $*s*_{1}, *s*_{2}, *x*_{1}, ..., *x*_{*n*}$ there are no two equal.

## Output

Output the only integer, minimum possible maximal distance between couriers during delivery.

## Note

In the first test case the initial distance between the couriers is $10$. This value will be the answer, for example, Petya can perform both deliveries, and Vasya will remain at the starting point.

In the second test case you can optimally act, for example, like this: Vasya delivers the package to the first customer, Petya to the second and, finally, Vasya delivers the package to the third client. With this order of delivery, the distance between the couriers will never exceed $1$.

In the third test case only two variants are possible: if the delivery of a single package is carried out by Petya, the maximum distance between them will be $5 - 2 = 3$. If Vasya will deliver the package, the maximum distance is $4 - 2 = 2$. The latter method is optimal.
statementZhMd:
Petya 和 Vasya 受雇成为快递员。在工作日内，他们需要将包裹配送到直线上的 $*n*$ 个不同地点。根据公司的内部规定，包裹必须严格按照特定顺序配送。最初，Petya 位于坐标为 $*s*_{1}$ 的点，Vasya 位于坐标为 $*s*_{2}$ 的点，而客户依次位于坐标为 $*x*_{1}, *x*_{2}, ..., *x*_{*n*}$ 的点，这也是要求的访问顺序。

两人会提前约定由谁为哪位客户配送包裹，然后按照以下方式行动。当第 $*i*$ 位客户的包裹送达后，负责为第 $(*i* + 1)$ 位客户配送包裹的人便出发前往目的地（可以是刚刚前往点 $*x*_{*i*}$ 的同一个人，也可以是另一个人）。没有负责当前包裹配送的那个人则停留在原地。

为了互相联系，两人配备了对讲机。但对讲机在距离较远时工作效果很差，因此 Petya 和 Vasya 希望合理分配配送任务，使得他们在工作期间的最大距离尽可能小。请帮助他们在遵守所有配送规则的前提下，最小化两名快递员之间的最大距离。

## 输入格式

第一行包含三个整数 $*n*$、$*s*_{1}$、$*s*_{2}$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 100 000$，$0 ≤ *s*_{1}, *s*_{2} ≤ 10^{9}$）——配送地点的数量，以及 Petya 和 Vasya 的初始位置。

第二行包含 $*n*$ 个整数 $*x*_{1}, *x*_{2}, ..., *x*_{*n*}$——客户的坐标，按照配送顺序给出（$0 ≤ *x*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$）。

保证在 $*s*_{1}$、$*s*_{2}$、$*x*_{1}, ..., *x*_{*n*}$ 中不存在两个相等的数。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数，即配送过程中两名快递员之间可能达到的最大距离的最小值。

## 说明

在第一个测试用例中，两名快递员的初始距离为 $10$。例如，可以由 Petya 完成两次配送，而 Vasya 一直留在起点，因此答案就是 $10$。

在第二个测试用例中，可以采取如下最优方案：Vasya 为第一位客户配送，Petya 为第二位客户配送，最后 Vasya 为第三位客户配送。在这种配送顺序下，两名快递员之间的距离始终不会超过 $1$。

在第三个测试用例中，只有两种方案：如果由 Petya 配送唯一的包裹，则两人之间的最大距离为 $5 - 2 = 3$；如果由 Vasya 配送，则最大距离为 $4 - 2 = 2$。后者是最优方案。
